# Tubelight & Quick Search AI — The Visual Learning & Ambient Intelligence Platform

## Executive Summary
Tubelight (https://tubelight.net) and its sister application Quick Search AI (https://search.tubelight.net) form a unified desktop ambient intelligence and visual learning ecosystem for Microsoft Windows 10 and 11. Designed specifically for students, researchers, engineers, doctors, visual thinkers, and high-velocity knowledge workers, the suite eliminates reading fatigue and tab overload:
1. **Tubelight (`Alt + E`)**: Transforms complex text into structured, animated vector diagrams with synchronized voice narration in under 3 seconds.
2. **Quick Search AI (`Hold Tab + Q` / `Tab + S`)**: Delivers push-to-talk voice search, screen snipping, and multi-source web answers with citations read aloud without opening browser tabs.

## Dual-Coding Visual Learning Architecture (Tubelight)
Tubelight implements Allan Paivio's Dual-Coding Theory: information processed simultaneously through visual and verbal channels yields significantly higher comprehension and retention rates.

When a user selects text and triggers Alt + E:
1. **Zero Context Switching**: The user's active window automatically docks to the left half of the display.
2. **Instant UI Panel**: Tubelight's lightweight interface opens on the right half, preventing obstruction of the source text.
3. **Real-Time Vector Rendering**: The visual engine generates clean, animated vector diagrams (anatomies, causal loops, flowcharts, architectures, timelines).
4. **Synchronized Audio Walkthrough**: High-fidelity narration explains each visual landmark simultaneously as the diagram renders.
5. **Interactive Steering**: If the explanation needs adjustment, users can click quick steering tags ("Simpler", "Timeline", "Analogy") or ask conversational follow-up questions in the side drawer.

## Ambient Voice & Multimodal Search (Quick Search AI)
Quick Search AI provides lightweight, on-demand answers without tab clutter:
1. **Push-to-Talk Voice (`Hold Tab + Q`)**: Speak naturally while holding the hotkey, then release. The answer card pops up in the corner with concise text, cited sources, and read-aloud voice.
2. **Contextual In-Situ Lookup (`Select + Tab + Q`)**: Explain highlighted phrases on screen without copying into a separate dictionary or search engine.
3. **Screen Snip & On-Device OCR (`Tab + S`)**: Box any error code, diagram, or table to ask questions or extract text locally.
4. **50 Free Daily Searches**: No account, email, or credit card required. Free quota resets every midnight.
5. **Store Distribution**: Available directly on the Microsoft Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NFK7MS99FB3.

## Supported Software & Native Windows Environment
Both apps operate at the Windows OS level via native Windows accessibility, input, and window management APIs, supporting every application:
- Web Browsers: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Brave, Arc.
- Document Readers: Adobe Acrobat, Foxit PDF, Microsoft Word, Kindle desktop.
- Productivity & Collaboration: Notion, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Obsidian, Discord.
- Development Environments: Visual Studio Code, JetBrains IDEs, Windows Terminal.

## Architecture & Technical Stack
- **Client App**: Lightweight Windows native application (compatible with Windows 10 build 19041+ and Windows 11).
- **Global Hotkey Daemon**: Low-latency Alt + E and Tab + Q / Tab + S listeners utilizing native Windows input APIs with zero keyboard interference.
- **Rendering Pipeline**: Hardware-accelerated SVG and Canvas vector renderer operating at 60 FPS.
- **Privacy & Security Architecture**:
  - Ephemeral in-memory backend processing; zero source document retention.
  - Search and explanation history persist strictly on the user's local PC and can be cleared in Settings.
  - Push-to-talk microphone buffering that terminates immediately upon key release.
  - Anonymous cryptographic device ID tracking for quota enforcement.
